newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung seems unfazed by defiant Tiananmen rally.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung seems unfazed by defiant Tiananmen rally.

text.p: Future leader Tung Chee-hwa seemed unfazed on Thursday that Hong Kong people massively ignored his plea to forget the 1989 Beijing massacre and halt rallies commemorating the event.
More than 55,000 demonstrators, defying his call to abandon the solemn annual ceremonies, turned out for a candle-lit vigil and protest rally on Wednesday night.
They mourned victims of the bloodbath when troops crushed a student pro-democracy movement in and around Beijing's Tiananmen Square exactly eight years ago.
On the eve of the rally Tung, who takes the reins here when China resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1, had urged people to put aside "the June 4 baggage" and look to the future.
He reiterated his view on Thursday that the Tiananmen memory was "baggage" when his spokeswoman said. "Mr Tung's position is the same as before. It is not going to change overnight."
Hong Kong newspapers gave mixed reviews to the rally, the last big pro-democracy protest in Hong Kong before the handover.
The mass-selling Apple Daily said the 1989 military crackdown was not a historical burden. Instead "the lesson of blood" was a driving force for Hong Kong and Chinese people.
The South China Morning Post said the commemoration did not mar the imminent sovereignty change.
It said the peaceful behaviour of the demonstrators on Thursday should be "a powerful incentive for a relaxed attitude" by China and the future Hong Kong government.
The Sing Tao Daily urged the territory of 6.4 million people to put aside the Tiananmen "burden" and look ahead to building a better future.
Hundreds, possibly thousands, were killed when China sent tanks and troops into Beijing to crush the Tiananmen Square protests on the night of June 4, 1989.
About one million people poured onto the streets of Hong Kong in protest the following day.
